pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. run
   C. quickly
   D. happiness

2. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

3. When practising Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

4. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

5. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

6. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

7. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only an action
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

9. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

10. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.

11. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. goed

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Phrasal Verbs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Writing process – dialogues 13.5.1 Narrative Composition 14.5.1 Descriptive writ and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — run

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

7. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

8. A — Where is the library?

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

11. A — went

12. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 12.3.1 Phrasal Verbs; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing process – dialogues 13.5.1 Narrative Composition 14.5.1 Descriptive writ; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
